judgments.title: SYARIKAT AIR MELAKA BERHAD v FASIHAH BINTI ZAMRAN & ors
judgments.catchwords: TORT — Negligence — Road obstruction — Motorcyclist colliding with unlit signboard on dark bend — Ownership and responsibility inferred from utility’s label and absence of explanation — Child pillion’s direct evidence supported by physical and contemporaneous evidence — Photographs of disturbed scene not establishing original position of board — Suggested pothole cause remaining speculative — Duty to place, maintain and remove signboard safely breached — Liability upheld. TORT — Contributory negligence — Burden on defendant — Pillion’s sighting of obstruction not establishing rider’s opportunity to avoid it — No evidence of speed, visibility distance, reaction time, braking distance or room to swerve — Inference of want of care based on hindsight — Helmet allegation unsupported — Finding of 10% contributory negligence set aside — Defendant wholly liable — Civil Law Act 1956, s 12(1). DAMAGES — Personal injuries — Severe traumatic brain injury — Permanent total dependency — Bedridden patient retaining awareness distinguished from persistent vegetative state — Global award covering neurological sequelae — RM400,000 within applicable Compendium range — Less disabling injuries unsuitable comparators — No basis for appellate reduction. DAMAGES — Special damages — Family’s travelling expenses during hospitalisation — Daily visits and reasonable journey cost established by uncontradicted oral evidence — Absence of receipts not fatal — Strict proof assessed according to nature of expenditure and available evidence — Award of RM2,200 upheld. DAMAGES — Loss of future earnings — Cash-paid worker at family food stall — Related witnesses’ evidence requiring assessment rather than rejection merely for relationship — Employment corroborated by medical histories and unchallenged testimony — Absence of wage records or statutory contributions not defeating claim — Statutory sixteen-year multiplier applied without further contingency deduction — RM215,040 awarded — Civil Law Act 1956, s 28A(2). DAMAGES — Future care — Full-time helper required on both parties’ expert evidence — Gratuitous care by mother not relieving tortfeasor of liability — Discretionary welfare payment not deductible — Recurring recruitment costs assessed over successive two-year contracts — Award reassessed at RM819,472. DAMAGES — Future medical expenses — Competing expert costings — Later assessment reflecting stabilised condition preferred — Supplier’s quotation proving price rather than required quantity — Nutrition, consumables and replacement equipment distinguished from free public hospital treatment — Possibility of government assistance not proof of assured provision — RM356,970 awarded. DAMAGES — Future care and medical expenses — Deduction for contingencies and accelerated receipt — Non-statutory multipliers distinguished from statutory earnings multiplier — Injury-specific survival tables already accounting for reduced life expectancy — Further mortality discount constituting double deduction — Accelerated receipt considered alongside absence of allowance for rising costs — Unreasoned one-third deductions set aside. CIVIL PROCEDURE — Appeal — Findings based on inference and assessment of expert evidence — Unsupported contributory negligence finding and rejection of earnings evidence on relationship alone — Unexplained choice of care costings — Appellate reassessment without remittal — Utility’s appeal dismissed and plaintiffs’ appeal allowed — Total damages varied to RM1,818,202.
judgments.judge: YA Dato' Sri Raja Segaran A/L S.Krishnan

judgments.title: LEE KUAH SHYAN v Lee Kuah Woon & ors
judgments.catchwords: Originating Summons for declaratory relief as to the true construction of the Last Will and Testament - testator’s intention as expressed in the words of the will read as a whole, and not his unexpressed subjective wishes - Second, the court will, so far as the language permits, prefer a construction that gives every clause some operative effect over one that renders any clause meaningless - where two constructions are reasonably open, and one produces an intestacy, be it whole or partial, while the other avoids it, the court prefers the construction that avoids intestacy - the court is not entitled to make a fresh will for the testator merely because it suspects that he did not mean what he plainly said - the court may inform itself of the testator’s actual circumstances at the time he made the will, this includes his family, his property, and his business relationships, to understand what he meant by the words he used, before concluding that those words are ambiguous or deciding how any ambiguity is to be resolved. - company is a legal person distinct from its members, and that a shareholder, even one holding practically the whole of the issued capital, has no legal or equitable proprietary interest in the company’s assets.

judgments.title: JCL CREDIT LEASING SDN. BHD. v OOI CHUNG YI
judgments.catchwords: Consequently, the action is dismissed. This dismissal is not a commentary on the parties’ broader commercial relationship, nor on the Plaintiff’s internal processes. It is a reflection of the legal reality that a pleading must disclose a complete, viable cause of action before the machinery of litigation can be invoked. Where that threshold is not met, the Court must intervene at the threshold stage to prevent the misuse of judicial resources and the unnecessary exposure of parties to litigation that cannot succeed even if all pleaded facts are assumed true. Costs are fixed at RM5,000.00, payable by the Plaintiff to the Defendant.
judgments.judge: YA Tuan Nixon Anak Kennedy Kumbong

judgments.title: ZULKEPLI BIN ISMAIL v Pendakwa Raya & ors
judgments.catchwords: UNDANG-UNDANG JENAYAH – Kanun Keseksaan [Akta 574] – Seksyen 376(2)(c) lawan Seksyen 376(2)(d) – Rogol – Ketiadaan pembuktian bagi elemen memberatkan "kehadiran orang lain" – Kuasa Mahkamah Rayuan untuk meminda sabitan di bawah Seksyen 316(b)(ii) Kanun Tatacara Jenayah (KTJ) kepada Seksyen 376(2)(d) di mana mangsa berumur di bawah 16 tahun – Elemen penetrasi dan ketiadaan kerelaan. UNDANG-UNDANG JENAYAH – Akta Kesalahan-Kesalahan Seksual Terhadap Kanak-Kanak 2017 [Akta 792] – Seksyen 14(a) dibaca bersama Seksyen 16 – Amang seksual fizikal – Perbuatan menyentuh payudara dan kemaluan mangsa oleh seseorang yang mempunyai hubungan amanah – Pembuktian intipati penting dan konsistensi keterangan mangsa. PROSEDUR JENAYAH – Campur Tangan Rayuan – Prinsip-prinsip yang mengawal campur tangan terhadap dapatan fakta oleh hakim bicara – Kredibiliti dan pembawaan (demeanour) saksi – Penilaian percanggahan kecil berbanding intipati matan pertuduhan. PROSEDUR JENAYAH – Pertuduhan – Seksyen 156 dan Seksyen 422(a) KTJ – Percanggahan atau ketidaktepatan dalam butiran (seperti lokasi/bilik sebenar) – Sama ada ia menyebabkan prejudis, mengelirukan tertuduh, atau mengakibatkan kegagalan keadilan. KETERANGAN – Kekompetenan dan Kredibiliti Saksi – Seksyen 118 dan Seksyen 133A Akta Keterangan 1950 – Saksi kanak-kanak yang mempunyai masalah pembelajaran ("lembam") – Keupayaan memahami soalan dan memberikan jawapan rasional – Perbezaan antara kefahaman bahasa harian berbanding istilah undang-undang (contohnya, "rogol", "cabul"). KETERANGAN – Fakta Relevan – Seksyen 8(2) Akta Keterangan 1950 – Kelakuan mangsa membuat aduan awal / laporan polis awal sebagai fakta relevan yang menyokong garis masa dan menjadikan versi pendakwaan lebih munasabah.
judgments.judge: YA Tuan Haji Azhar Bin Mokhtar

judgments.catchwords: CONSTITUTIONAL LAW: Citizenship – Citizenship by operation of law – Child born in Malaysia – Biological parents remain unidentified – Whether Child was “found exposed” under section 19B of Part III of the Second Schedule – Broad meaning of “found exposed” – Whether constitutional presumption arose – Whether Defendants rebutted presumption – Whether Child satisfies section 1(a) read with section 19B – Whether Child satisfies section 1(e) read with section 2(3) – Whether absence of identified foreign citizenship sufficient to establish prima facie case – Whether lawful adoptive parents fall within “parents” under section 1(a) – Effect of Adoption Order – Whether pending Article 15A application renders Originating Summons premature – Whether administrative alteration of birth record affects citizenship by operation of law – Plaintiffs succeed on Issues 1 and 2 but fail on Issue 3 – Originating Summons allowed.

judgments.title: Pendakwa Raya & ors v Julasiri Bin Akilmara
judgments.catchwords: Offence under section 39B(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 read together with section 34 of the Penal Code - Whether the trial judge should have informed at the close of the prosecution's case, that the defence was being called upon to answer a case of actual trafficking or presumed trafficking? - Overwhelming evidence proved the elements of custody, control, and knowledge - Actual possession of the impugned drugs was established - Section 180 (1) and (4) of the Criminal Procedure Code - Procedure after conclusion of case for prosecution - No statutory or legal requirement to state the presumption when calling for the defence - Formal verbal label for an evidentiary rule at the close of the prosecution's case is unnecessary - Statutory presumption of trafficking under section 37(da)(xvi) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 - Section 422 of the Criminal Procedure Code - Not vitiate the conviction - No miscarriage of justice - Failure either to make or to record such a finding does not ipso facto - The law does not require a mini-judgment or detailed legal reasons at the close of the prosecution’s case
